frameworks.name: Mastra
best_for: TypeScript teams building agents, workflows and RAG in one codebase
Node or serverless deployments that share types with a React front end
Built-in durable workflows, tool calling, memory and evaluation hooks
avoid_when: The delivery team is Python or JVM based
The customer requires a framework with a long enterprise support history
frameworks.notes: Open-source TypeScript agent framework. Provider-agnostic model access, typed tools and step-based workflows. Good fit when the whole solution is TypeScript.

frameworks.name: LangChain
best_for: Chains with structured output where the work is sequential
Swapping model providers behind one interface
Wide connector coverage for loaders, retrievers and vector stores
avoid_when: The flow is a single model call with no branching; the abstraction adds no value
The team needs stable, long-lived APIs and cannot absorb version churn
frameworks.notes: Large ecosystem and many integrations. Best used as a thin layer for model access, structured output and retrieval rather than as an application framework.

frameworks.name: LangGraph
best_for: Explicit state machines with branching, loops and validate-then-repair cycles
Long-running flows that need checkpointing, resume and human-in-the-loop pauses
Multi-agent designs where control flow must be inspectable
avoid_when: The workflow is linear and deterministic; a plain function is clearer
The team is not comfortable modelling explicit graph state
frameworks.notes: Graph runtime from the LangChain project. Adds durable state, interrupts and replay. Pairs with LangChain for the model and retrieval layer.

frameworks.name: Semantic Kernel
best_for: .NET estates already using Microsoft identity, hosting and tooling
Plugin and function-calling patterns with dependency injection
Solutions that will be operated by a Microsoft-centric platform team
avoid_when: The delivery stack is Node or Python-first with no .NET presence
The customer wants to stay deliberately cloud-neutral
frameworks.notes: Microsoft's agent and orchestration SDK. Strongest when the target platform is Azure and Microsoft Foundry, where the operational model matches the rest of the estate.

frameworks.name: Vercel AI SDK
best_for: Streaming model output into a React, Next.js or Svelte interface
Token-by-token UI, tool-call rendering and generative UI components
Provider-agnostic model calls from a web front end or edge runtime
avoid_when: The orchestration is server-side, long-running and stateful
The back end is Python or JVM and only the UI is TypeScript
frameworks.notes: A model and streaming layer for web applications, not a workflow engine. Often combined with a server-side orchestrator rather than used alone.

frameworks.name: Spring AI
best_for: Existing Spring Boot services that must add AI features in place
Reusing Spring configuration, observability, security and testing conventions
JVM teams that will own the solution long term
avoid_when: There is no existing JVM platform and no JVM skills in the delivery team
The design needs fast-moving agent features ahead of the Spring release cadence
frameworks.notes: Brings model calls, structured output, advisors and vector stores into the Spring programming model. The main argument for it is operational fit with an existing Java estate.

frameworks.name: LlamaIndex
best_for: Retrieval-heavy solutions over large, mixed document sets
Ingestion, chunking, metadata filtering and multi-stage retrieval with reranking
Evaluating retrieval quality separately from generation quality
avoid_when: Retrieval is a single vector lookup that the cloud platform already provides
The main problem is orchestration and tool use rather than retrieval
frameworks.notes: Focused on the indexing and retrieval half of a RAG solution. Frequently combined with a separate orchestration layer.

frameworks.name: Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
best_for: AWS-standard customers who want models, guardrails and agent runtime under one bill and one IAM model
Managed retrieval via Bedrock Knowledge Bases without running an indexing pipeline
Content filtering and PII redaction through Bedrock Guardrails as a platform control
avoid_when: The customer requires portability across clouds or self-hosted open-weight models
A needed model or model version is not offered in the required region
frameworks.notes: Managed AWS AI service family. The strongest argument is operational: existing AWS identity, networking, logging and procurement apply unchanged.

frameworks.name: Microsoft Foundry
best_for: Azure-standard customers using Microsoft Entra ID, private networking and Azure Policy
Managed agents, evaluation and tracing through Foundry Agent Service and Foundry observability
Retrieval built on Azure AI Search with hybrid and semantic ranking
avoid_when: The customer wants cloud-neutral deployment or self-hosted inference
Regional model availability does not meet a data-residency requirement
frameworks.notes: Managed Azure AI platform, formerly Azure AI Foundry. Covers the model catalog, agent runtime, evaluation and content safety with Azure-native governance.

frameworks.name: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
best_for: Google Cloud customers whose data already sits in BigQuery or Cloud Storage
Managed retrieval through Agent Search and Vertex AI Vector Search
Model evaluation, tuning and endpoint management inside one platform
avoid_when: The customer requires model portability or on-premises inference
The team has no Google Cloud operating experience
frameworks.notes: Managed Google Cloud AI platform, formerly Vertex AI. Includes the Agent Development Kit for building agents and Model Armor for prompt and response screening.

frameworks.name: Custom orchestration
best_for: A small, fixed number of well-understood model calls
Strict control over prompts, retries, timeouts and structured-output validation
Minimising dependencies where the customer's security review is strict
avoid_when: The design needs durable state, resume, branching and human-in-the-loop pauses
The team would end up rebuilding a framework under a different name
frameworks.notes: Direct provider SDK calls behind the team's own interfaces. Lowest dependency footprint and easiest to reason about, at the cost of writing state handling, retries and evaluation plumbing.
